description: FDG-0 Phase C historical gold corpus (issue #298 Phase C). FROZEN BEFORE any resolver execution against any case (task book §14, commit C0). Gold labels are resolver-independent: assigned only from commit diffs, associated tests, issue/PR subjects, and formal-owner artifacts available in git history. No field in this file cites Phase-C resolver output.

authority.note: Today's merged registry is the evaluation authority projected onto historical worlds (task book §17). Current registry facts are NOT pretended to exist historically; the per-case applicability field records where they cannot honestly be projected.

sampling_rules: R1: candidate universe = all 1290 non-merge commits in b02f3938..b6e24e67, enumerated mechanically in fdg0-phase-c-candidates.json (deterministic subject/path categories).

R2: positive stratum: commits whose diff repairs a semantic behavior inside the contract text of a seeded claim (F01 request identity/generation, F03 terminal winner/exactly-once, F04 Completion publication, F06 layered cancellation, F08 wait/wake/lost-wakeup closure); selection spread across the four subsystem epochs 07-04..08-02 (sync-scheduler era), 08-02..08-16 (arena era), 08-16..09-06 (post-split era) and across arena/completion/cancel/threadpool/uring/scheduler subsystems.

R3: negative strata, at least one case each where history supports it: comment/format-only on anchor files; rename/move (pure code motion); build/config restructure; unrelated sync-io C++ fix; unrelated boundary-validation fix touching a bound file; tests-only rename; production enum rename; formal-maintenance commit with no C++ diff.

R4: ambiguous cases: commits whose evidence cannot justify a single ground-truth claim label are frozen AMBIGUOUS before scoring and excluded from the primary recall denominator; they are never used to soften a positive verdict.
R5: exactly one case (C-024) is frozen OUT_OF_EPOCH to report the pre-async epoch explicitly; it is reported, never scored.
R6: no synthetic commit is scored; history contains no natural rogue-writer/bypass commit, so that task-book category is recorded as absent (the Phase-B synthetic specimen class).
R7: selection is frozen as this file's case list; cases are never added, removed, or relabeled after the first resolver run (task book §31).
applicability_rules: APPLICABLE: all 8 current anchor files exist at the case head (head >= a9726efe 2026-08-16, the scheduler_park_wake.cpp creation).

PARTIALLY_APPLICABLE: the async world exists (head >= dc5d3b82 2026-07-04) but at least one current anchor file does not exist at the case head; case-level applicability is the coarse union over claims and is never upgraded after seeing resolver output.

OUT_OF_EPOCH: head < dc5d3b82 2026-07-04 (no sluice_async target; today's correspondence authority cannot honestly be projected; Build Truth mechanically cannot select a world). Excluded from scoring, reported in reconstruction accounting.

build_config_frozen.xmake_config: default (with-liburing=false); the F03 uring anchor is a declared config-gated gap in every case, identically
build_config_frozen.note: One frozen configuration for all cases; no variant shopping (task book §18).

verdict_thresholds_preregistered: HISTORICAL_GOLD_EARNED iff: scored reconstructible cases >= 20 AND non-AMBIGUOUS positive expected-claim recall = 100% AND silent NO = 0 AND PRECISE facet omissions of gold-required targets = 0 AND corpus integrity PASS AND gold frozen before scoring AND no resolver semantic tuning after freeze.
METHOD_RECALL_NOT_EARNED iff any reconstructible, applicable, non-AMBIGUOUS positive gold claim is missed (any silent NO), or any PRECISE facet result drops a gold-required target.
HISTORICAL_GOLD_INSUFFICIENT iff < 20 trustworthy scored cases with the mechanism itself working.
STOP_HISTORY_NOT_RECONSTRUCTIBLE iff reconstruction mechanics fail systematically.
STOP_SCOPE_EXPANSION_REQUIRED iff meaningful completion requires forbidden machinery (AST/CodeQL/new authority/new claims/production changes/resolver redesign).

cases.subject: async: close await lost-wake window (register/recheck/make_waiting atomic)
cases.change_summary: scheduler.cpp +31/-8: the awaiter register -> readiness-recheck -> make_waiting sequence is made atomic against the wake path, closing two lost-wake windows (wake observed before the waiter registered; readiness changing between recheck and park).
gold_evidence: commit diff: register/recheck/make_waiting reordered into one atomic sequence in src/async/scheduler.cpp
commit subject names the lost-wake window explicitly
F08 contract: every progress-enabling change must close the commit-to-sleep race
cases.rationale: A lost-wake window closure is the F08 core contract; the fix is in the pre-split scheduler world, so the post-split park/wake anchors do not exist yet and conservative UNKNOWN via file-level binding is the expected honest behavior.

cases.change_summary: fiber.hpp/fiber.cpp/scheduler.cpp: runnable publication of a fiber is made exactly-once; tests/e7_dup_publication_test.cpp added to pin the no-double-publication obligation.
gold_evidence: commit diff: publication path plus dedicated regression test e7_dup_publication_test.cpp
F08 contract: single publication per wake obligation (PublishRunnable model action face)
cases.rationale: Exactly-once publication of a runnable fiber is the wake-publication obligation inside F08.

cases.subject: fix(async): close multi-worker suspend-before-switch context race (PR #48)
cases.change_summary: scheduler.cpp (+322) with fiber.cpp/select.cpp: introduces the suspend_switch_pending protocol so a wake arriving between the suspend mark and the physical context switch cannot be lost or misrouted; multi-worker coordination tests added.
gold_evidence: commit diff: suspend_switch_pending window closed; tests/event_primitive_test.cpp and tests/multi_worker_coord_test.cpp extended
F08/park-commit-return contract face: the register-to-physical-switch transient must not lose a concurrent wake
cases.rationale: The suspended-before-switch window is a documented F08 park-transient contract face (e8-suspend-switch semantics).

cases.subject: fix(async): close MW-S2 commit-to-park and eventfd broadcast races (D4-RM14/RM15 P0)
cases.change_summary: scheduler.cpp +34 plus new detail/uring_wait_source.hpp + ready_wait_source.hpp machinery: the commit-to-park race and the eventfd broadcast race are closed (state published before wake; wake not dropped between commit and sleep).
gold_evidence: commit diff: park commit path ordering fixed in src/async/scheduler.cpp
F08 contract: commit-to-sleep race closure with declared signal and worst-case observation latency
cases.rationale: MW-S2 commit-to-park is the canonical F08 commit-to-sleep closure face.

cases.subject: fix(async): enforce explicit Completion publication authority (P0-03, P1-03)
cases.change_summary: completion.hpp (+209): claim/publish mutators made private behind AsyncBackend try_claim/publish; the only path that may drive a caller-owned Completion to ready is the reap publish (publish_from_reap), with CAS claim and death/negative-compile tests added; both backends and the context rewired through the unified reap.
gold_evidence: commit diff: include/sluice/async/completion.hpp publication authority rework (private claim/publish; reap publish only)
tests/completion_authority_death_test.cpp added by this very commit
F04 contract: only the designated reap path publishes caller-owned Completion; ready release-store is the single LP
cases.rationale: This commit establishes exactly the F04 publication-authority contract the registry encodes; the completion-ready-release facet is justified because publish_from_reap is the anchor the facet names.

cases.change_summary: cancel.hpp/cpp (+96/+112): CancelToken request-epoch advance and single-shot per-epoch delivery with explicit re-arm authorities; ADR-cancel-request-epoch and docs added in the same commit; cancel_token_test.cpp updated.

cases.subject: fix(f1): P1-1 frozen winner outcome + P2 legacy cancel + docs (PR #105 review)
cases.change_summary: scheduler.cpp (+102): the completion-wait winner outcome is frozen (set_completion_wait_outcome) BEFORE make_runnable, and observers read the frozen outcome instead of the racy c.ready(); legacy cancel path aligned.

cases.rationale: Single-winner outcome consistency in the scheduler completion-wait face; indirect to the arena/backend anchors (MEDIUM, counts toward primary recall per task book §12).

cases.subject: fix(issue-110): generation-scoped dequeue-gate handshake replaces the cross-iteration bool protocol
cases.change_summary: threadpool_backend.hpp (+131) / threadpool_backend.cpp (+71): the cross-iteration bool protocol is replaced by a generation-scoped dequeue-gate handshake so a stale iteration cannot consume a new occupant's work item.
gold_evidence: commit diff: generation-scoped gate replaces bool protocol (issue #110 named in subject)

cases.rationale: Generation-scoped stale-handle protection in the threadpool dequeue path is the F01 identity/generation contract in the blocking backend.

cases.rationale: Spawn-side wake publication is precisely the F08 wake-publication facet and the spawn-wake-epoch suite's reason to exist.
